- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct quickly; reduce forecast slope in subsequent days.
- When sentiment is neutral or flat (all 0.00), model exhibits persistent overconfidence; dampen forecast volatility and anchor to recent 7–14 day moving average.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast exceeds 2 standard deviations above recent mean, reduce by 10–15%.
- If true outcome shows downward trend after forecast peak, model often fails to recognize it; add lagged correction: if true price drops >5% from forecast peak, reduce next forecast by 5–8%.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model overweights historical momentum; reduce weight of recent 3–5 day highs in smoothing.
